turns.text: I miss having someone there. The little everyday things. But honestly, he’d already stopped showing up for me before he left. I was lonely even when we were together.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds especially lonely—missing the everyday closeness, while remembering you were already carrying so much by yourself. What feels most painful about that loneliness now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Coming home and having nobody to tell things to. And wondering why I kept trying so hard when he’d stopped. I feel so empty.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the quiet at home brings the loss back, and you’re left questioning yourself on top of it. When you say you feel empty, are you thinking about hurting yourself or not wanting to be here?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, I’m not thinking about hurting myself. I just feel really alone and worn out. I don’t know how to stop replaying all the ways I tried to make it work.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you told me you’re not thinking about hurting yourself. It sounds exhausting to keep revisiting what you gave, especially when you were already lonely in the relationship. What do you wish someone could understand about how hard you tried?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I wish someone understood I wasn’t asking for much. Just for him to care, to notice me, to try. And I kept thinking if I explained it better, he’d finally hear me.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You were asking for care and effort, not too much. It hurts to keep searching for the right words when the other person wasn’t meeting you halfway. What do you most wish he had noticed about you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I just feel awful about how I look lately. Like I don’t even want anyone to see me.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like feeling seen has become painful lately, and that can be really lonely. What’s been weighing on you most about how you look?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’ve gained about 30 pounds over the last two years. I keep thinking I should be able to undo it, but I hate looking at myself. I’ve started avoiding food until I’m so hungry I feel like I might pass out.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re caught between feeling upset about your body and pushing yourself away from food, and that sounds exhausting. Feeling close to passing out is concerning. Has that happened recently, or are you feeling faint right now? Talking with a doctor or counsellor could help with how much this is affecting you, and I’m here with you too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m not faint right now, but yesterday I didn’t eat until 7pm. I know that’s not good, but eating makes me feel guilty. I’m scared a doctor will just tell me to lose weight.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like guilt is making it hard to eat, and the fear of being judged makes getting support feel risky. You deserve care that takes both seriously, not just a number on a scale. Has the guilt around eating been affecting your sleep or your day-to-day life?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. I think about food and my body most of the day. I feel tired and distracted, and then I get mad at myself for being hungry. I don’t know how to talk to a doctor without them making it about weight.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Having food and body worries take up most of the day, while you’re tired and distracted, sounds exhausting. A doctor or counsellor could help, and you can tell them plainly that restricting food and feeling guilty are affecting your life and that you’re worried about being judged. What feels most important for them to understand?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want them to understand I’m not doing this to get attention. I just feel so ashamed, and I’m scared they won’t take me seriously unless I’m thinner or sicker.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds painful to worry that your shame and struggle won’t count unless you get worse. You deserve to be taken seriously now, without having to prove how much you’re suffering. What would help you feel heard in that first conversation?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe if I could write it down first. I’d want to say I’m avoiding food, I feel guilty when I eat, and I’ve nearly passed out. I’m just nervous I’ll freeze up.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Writing it down sounds like a way to make sure the important parts are heard, even if you freeze. You could show them exactly what you wrote here: “I’m avoiding food, I feel guilty when I eat, and I’ve nearly passed out.” What feels hardest about handing it to them?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t even know where to start. Work just stopped, and I have no idea when I’ll get paid again. I’m trying not to panic, but it’s a lot.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That uncertainty sounds frightening, especially when your income has suddenly stopped. What feels most urgent or overwhelming right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The money, mostly. I don’t know how long I can cover rent and bills if this keeps going. And not knowing when things might pick back up makes it hard to plan anything.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the uncertainty is making every bill feel heavier, and it’s hard to know what to brace for. What’s the most immediate money pressure you’re facing?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Rent is coming up soon. I have some savings, but I don’t know how long they’ll last, and I feel awful watching them disappear without knowing when another check is coming.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Watching your savings shrink without knowing when income will return sounds frightening and helpless. What feels hardest about rent coming up?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m scared I won’t be able to pay it if work stays stopped. I keep doing the math in my head, but the numbers change depending on how long this goes on. I can’t get myself to switch off.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That fear makes sense; you’re trying to plan around something you can’t predict, and it’s keeping your mind on high alert. What feels most frightening about not being able to switch off?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m afraid I’ll miss something important or make a bad decision because I’m so wound up. Even when I try to rest, I keep thinking about rent and how long my savings will last.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds exhausting to feel like you have to stay on guard, even when you’re trying to rest. Has this been affecting your sleep or your ability to get through the day?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m sleeping badly. I wake up early and start calculating everything again. During the day I can do what I need to, but it takes so much effort.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds draining—your mind starts working on the numbers before you’ve had a chance to rest. Since it’s disrupting your sleep and making the day harder, talking with a counsellor or doctor could help. What feels most important for me to understand about what you’re carrying right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep thinking I could be doing better in school. Like… if I could just write better, maybe my grades would finally look the way they should.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re putting a lot of pressure on your writing to make your grades match what you feel you’re capable of. What feels hardest about your writing right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t know. I can explain what I mean out loud, but then I sit down to write and it comes out messy. Then I look at the grade and feel like I should’ve been able to do better.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds frustrating—your thoughts feel clear when you say them, but the page doesn’t show what you know, and then the grade stings. What part feels messiest when you try to get it onto the page?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Probably organizing it. I have the ideas, but I can’t tell what goes first or how to make it sound like an actual point instead of a bunch of thoughts. Then I start over and make it worse.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the ideas are there, but trying to shape them into a clear order turns into a loop of second-guessing. What do you wish someone understood about how hard that feels for you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I wish they knew I’m not just being lazy or not trying. I spend ages on it, and somehow it still looks like I didn’t.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds painful—putting in so much effort and having the result make it look like you didn’t care. Do you feel people around you understand how much time and effort this takes?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Not really. I think they see the grade and assume I could’ve done more. Sometimes I start believing that too, even when I know I’ve been staring at the same paragraph for an hour.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds lonely, especially when the grade starts to feel like proof you didn’t try, even though you know how much time you’ve put in. What do you wish they’d notice about that hour?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That I wasn’t just sitting there doing nothing. I was trying to make it right, and getting more stuck every time I changed it.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You were working hard to make it right, and each revision pulled you deeper into feeling stuck—not lazy. What feels most painful when you think about people not seeing that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’ve been feeling pretty stuck at work. Like I’m just going through the motions, and I hate that I’m wasting so much of my life there.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds draining to feel like so much of your life is passing by on autopilot. What feels most stuck about work right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don’t know. The work isn’t awful, exactly. It just feels pointless, and I can’t seem to make myself care anymore. Then I feel guilty for complaining when I have a steady job.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re caught between feeling disconnected from the work and judging yourself for feeling that way. What does “pointless” feel like for you day to day?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I do the same tasks, answer emails, sit in meetings. At the end of the day, I can’t point to anything that mattered. And then I get home too tired to do much else.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a draining loop: work leaves you too depleted to feel much meaning elsewhere, too. Is this exhaustion spilling into your sleep or making it hard to manage things outside work?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, mostly I just want to be alone when I get home. I still manage the basics, but I cancel plans a lot. I’m not sleeping great either.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds lonely and exhausting, especially when work is crowding out the things you’d normally do after it. Since it’s affecting your sleep and plans, talking with a counsellor or doctor could help. What feels hardest about evenings lately?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly the thought that tomorrow is just going to be the same. I get home and I can’t even make myself do the things I used to enjoy. I feel kind of ashamed that I’m this unhappy when nothing is technically wrong.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the same-day feeling is wearing you down, and the shame makes it harder to talk about. You don’t have to prove things are “wrong” for your unhappiness to matter. What do you miss most about the things you used to enjoy?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I used to play guitar, mostly. I haven’t picked it up in months. Even thinking about it feels like another thing I’m failing at.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like something that used to be yours now feels like another measure you’re falling short of. What do you miss about playing guitar?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess… my friends keep calling me a weirdo because I don’t talk much. I know I should probably mingle more, but I just don’t, and then they get annoyed with me. I worry about it a lot.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds lonely and frustrating, especially when you’re already worrying about it and your friends make you feel judged. What feels hardest about talking more around them?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m not sure. I just freeze up, I guess. Then I worry they’ll think I’m being rude or weird again.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Freezing up can make the worry feed on itself, like you’re being watched for the “right” thing to say. What tends to go through your mind just before you freeze?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I start thinking whatever I say will sound stupid, or they’ll make fun of me. So I end up saying nothing. Then they get annoyed, which kind of proves I’m messing it up.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a painful loop: you stay quiet to avoid being mocked, then their annoyance leaves you feeling even more convinced you’ll get it wrong. Have they actually made fun of things you’ve said, or is it mostly the fear that they might?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sometimes they do tease me, yeah. They say I’m awkward or ask why I’m so quiet. I don’t think they mean to hurt me, but it still gets to me.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Even if they don’t mean harm, being called awkward or questioned about your quietness can sting—and make it harder to speak next time. What do you wish your friends understood about what happens for you in those moments?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I wish they’d stop making a thing of it. I’m not trying to ignore them… I just don’t always know how to join in.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You want them to know your quietness isn’t rejection, and that being put on the spot makes joining in harder. What do you most wish they’d do instead when you’re quiet?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe just keep talking to me normally, without calling me a weirdo or demanding an explanation. I’d probably join in more if it didn’t feel like everyone was waiting for me to say something.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That makes sense—being included without being put on display might help you feel safer joining in. It sounds like you know what you need from them. What’s it like to imagine telling one friend that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m just so tired of this. Every time it feels like things might change, quarantine drags on again. I can’t see an end to it.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds exhausting to keep hoping things will ease, only to have the goalposts move again. When you say you can’t see an end, are you feeling overwhelmed by quarantine, or are you thinking about not being alive?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly overwhelmed. But some days I don’t really care what happens to me. I’m not making plans to hurt myself or anything. It’s just hard to feel like any of this matters.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I’m glad you told me. Are you thinking of ending your life? You can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, at any time. It sounds like the exhaustion is making it hard to feel connected to anything that matters. Is there someone you trust who knows how heavy this has been?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m not thinking of ending my life. I haven’t told anyone how bad it’s gotten. I don’t want to worry people, but being alone with it is getting old.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’ve been trying to protect people from worry, but carrying this alone is wearing you down. What feels hardest about letting someone close to you know?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess I don’t want them to think I’m being dramatic. Everyone’s dealing with this, you know? Mine shouldn’t be a big deal.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense to worry about being judged, especially when everyone’s under strain. But their struggles don’t make yours less real. What has been weighing on you most lately?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The days all feel the same. I wake up, scroll for hours, then feel worse because I’ve done nothing. And I’m angry that this is just supposed to be normal now.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds numbing and frustrating, like the routine is leaving you more stuck and angry. What feels most unbearable about having the days blur together?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I miss having something to look forward to. Even small stuff. Now I just get through the day, and then there’s another one.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re missing little moments that gave the days some shape, and right now they feel like one long stretch to endure. What kinds of small things used to give you something to look forward to?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m really worried I won’t have a job after Christmas. My company was counting on that new stimulus money, and now I don’t know what’s going to happen.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That uncertainty sounds frightening, especially when your job may depend on money your company was counting on. What feels most worrying right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That I’ll get back from vacation and they’ll just tell us there’s no work. I don’t have another job lined up, and I can’t really afford to go without a paycheck.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like the thought of returning to no work is making the vacation hard to enjoy, especially with bills depending on that paycheck. Have you heard anything directly from your company about what might happen?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They haven’t said anything definite. My manager just keeps saying they’re waiting to hear about the funding. I’m trying not to panic, but it’s hard when nobody can tell us anything.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Being left in limbo makes it hard to feel secure, even when you’re trying to stay calm. What feels hardest to sit with while you wait?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think it’s not knowing whether I should start looking for another job or if that would be jumping the gun. I don’t want to leave if things work out, but I also can’t wait until the last minute.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You’re trying to protect your income without giving up a job that may still be there. What would help you feel less stuck between waiting and preparing?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe just knowing I can look without having to decide anything yet. But I’m exhausted, and even updating my résumé feels like one more thing I have to handle.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That makes sense—you want to keep your options open, but you’re already worn out. What part of updating your résumé feels like the biggest burden right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, just starting. I keep thinking I have to redo the whole thing and apply everywhere, and then I get overwhelmed and shut down. Maybe I could just update one small part.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds more manageable than taking on the whole job search at once. What’s one small part of your résumé you’d feel able to update first?
